# Writing a script

Every mark a Generative or Synthesis script, or a Table brief, may carry - the list the script editor's palette (**Edit** on the panel) is built from, and the patterns it highlights with. A script is Markdown; YAML frontmatter at the top is the panel's and never shown in the editor or spoken. A Table brief is handed to the show's agents rather than read aloud, so a mark offered there says what it does in a brief.

ScriptMarks - every authoring mark a script may carry, registered with what it does.

A script is plain Markdown, and ghost reads more out of it than the words: speaker cues, hesitations, picture markers, inline pronunciations, template macros, emphasis. Each of those used to be documented only where it was implemented, so a new author had no way to find out what ghost understands short of reading the source. This is the one list: the `ScriptWriter` palette is built from it, `ScriptHighlighter` colors a script with its patterns, and docs.py writes docs/script.md from it.

AN ENTRY DOES NOT IMPLEMENT ITS MARK. The parsers of record stay where they are (`Manuscript` for cues, rests and pictures; `TextNorm` and `Phonemes` for the rest), and `tests/notes/script_marks_check.gd` inserts every entry's example and asks THOSE parsers what they make of it - so an entry that drifts from what the reader actually does fails there, and a new entry without a check fails too.

A CARDS BRIEF IS NOT A SCRIPT, AND HAS MARKS OF ITS OWN (2026-10-12, the user: "why are all of the supported macros and features missing from 'cards' editor mode? I would expect that most if not all of the features from generative mode should also work here"). The palette was empty there because no entry named the mode: a show's document is the BRIEF its agents work from, never read aloud, so a mark in it does something only where the code reads it out of the brief or an agent is told to honor it. Those are offered ("table" in `modes`), each saying what it does THERE (`blurbs`): a speaker cue gives the show another voice, a `## Cards` section is its deck, a macro reads as its default and a note to self is taken out before any agent sees the brief (`TablePrompts.brief`), and a hesitation, a delivery or a stressed word stands in a line the brief gives the host word for word (rules/table/reader.yaml, `spoken`). The marks of a page or a tablet (pictures, scene lines, web pages) and the inline pronunciation are not: the table is the only medium there, its pictures are the painter's, and a reader's passage keeps no bracket (`TableProducer.clean_spoken`).

Registry: `ScriptMarks.REGISTRY` in [src/notes/script_marks.gd](../src/notes/script_marks.gd) (44 entries). Each one is proven against the parser that reads it by `tests/notes/script_marks_check.gd`.

## Voices

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speaker cue | `<!-- speaker: Name -->` | Generative, Table | Hands everything after it to the named voice, until the next cue. The panel's voices list follows the names the script uses. Must be a line of its own, or it is only a note. **In a Table brief:** Gives the show another voice by this name: a tab of its own on the Voice card, and the reader writes its lines and hands them over. Say in the brief who it is and when it speaks. Must be a line of its own. |

## Timing

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hesitation | `<!-- hesitation -->` | Generative, Table | A longer rest at exactly this point, mid-sentence included. Its length is the panel's Hesitate dial. **In a Table brief:** In a line the brief gives the host to say word for word, a rest at exactly this point; its length is the Voice card's Hesitate dial. Everywhere else the reader places its own. |
| Delivery | `<!-- delivery: quicker, brighter -->` | Generative, Table | Lean how the rest of this paragraph is said, a step at a time: quicker / slower, brighter / graver, tighter / looser (pauses), louder / softer, or excited, serious, hushed, urgent, playful, tender, dry; steady is the voice's own. Small, and eased in and out over a few sentences. **In a Table brief:** On a line of its own before words the brief gives the host to say word for word: leans how they are said - quicker / slower, brighter / graver, tighter / looser, louder / softer, or excited, serious, hushed, urgent, playful, tender, dry. Everywhere else the reader chooses its own. |
| Timed hesitation | `<!-- hesitation: 2.5 -->` | Generative, Table | A rest of exactly this many seconds, whatever the Hesitate dial says. **In a Table brief:** In a line the brief gives the host to say word for word, a rest of exactly this many seconds. |
| Log-entry time | `21:40` | Generative | A time opening a paragraph is read as its heading, with a hesitation after it. The Notebook sets it in the margin. |
| Thinking hum | `Hmm.` | Generative | Hm, Hmm, Mmm as a sentence of their own are held to most of a second, settling and falling in pitch, instead of read as a clipped syllable. |
| Outro starts here | `<!-- outro -->` | Generative | The end begins at this point: the reading carries on but fades out - voice and picture together, over the Outro setting - and whatever text is left is cut. Own line or mid-sentence; the first one counts. |

## Pictures

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Picture | `<!-- image: what the picture shows -->` | Generative | An illustration, described, placed where it sits: a full page when it opens the chapter or a scene, beside the text otherwise. Generated on request in the Illustrations panel. |
| Full-page picture | `<!-- image (full): what the picture shows -->` | Generative | A picture pinned to a page of its own, wherever it sits. |
| Picture, left edge | `<!-- image (left): what the picture shows -->` | Generative | A picture beside the text, pinned to the left edge. (right) and (inline) pin it the other ways. |
| Sketch | `<!-- sketch: a wiring diagram -->` | Generative | A drawing made on the page in the writer's own ink, black on white, without the book's style or references. |

## Pronunciation

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pronunciation | `[K AE T]` | Generative, Synthesis | Spells a word in ARPAbet phonemes, read exactly as written. For a name the voice gets wrong. |
| Letter | `[a]` | Generative, Synthesis | A letter that names something - a number, a point, a case - said by its name and shown as the letter: [a] is "ay", where a bare a is read as the word a. |

## Text

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Template macro | `${CHAPTERS_BEFORE:twenty-one}` | Generative, Synthesis, Table | A placeholder for a fact only the book's build knows. Ghost Notes reads the default after the colon, never the macro itself; one with no default is skipped and named in the panel. **In a Table brief:** A placeholder for a fact only the build knows. The agents are handed the default after the colon, never the macro itself; one with no default is left out. |

## Typography

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Heading | `# Heading` | Generative, Synthesis, Table | Spoken like any line, set as a heading on the page. The frontmatter's title is read first on its own. **In a Table brief:** A section of the brief, for the agents to find their way by. One heading is read by Ghost Notes itself: Cards, the show's deck. |
| Scene line | `*Nine-thirty. Orientation.*` | Generative | A short paragraph entirely in italics announces a change of time or place; a picture just before it gets a full page. |
| Italic | `*emphasized*` | Generative, Synthesis, Table | Shown in italics in the subtitles and on the page, and a word or a few so marked is hit: held longer and said louder. A longer run is typography, said plainly. The asterisks are never spoken. **In a Table brief:** In a line the brief gives the host to say word for word, the word the voice hits, shown in italics in the subtitle. Anywhere else it is emphasis for the agents reading the brief. |
| Bold | `**strong**` | Generative, Synthesis, Table | Shown in bold in the subtitles and on the page, and a word or a few so marked is hit harder than an italic one. The asterisks are never spoken. **In a Table brief:** In a line the brief gives the host to say word for word, the word the voice hits hardest, shown in bold in the subtitle. Anywhere else it is emphasis for the agents reading the brief. |
| Scene break | `* * *` | Generative | A rule across the page between two scenes. Silent. |

## Tablet

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web page | `<!-- url: www.example.com -->` | Generative | Tablet: the page below lives at this address. How it is reached is worked out - a link on the page on screen is tapped, anything else is typed in. With nothing written under it, it is the REAL page there, captured from the web. |
| Search | `<!-- search: what is the 7th realm -->` | Generative | Tablet: type this into a search box - the page's own, on a search engine, else the address bar - and the results page follows. |
| New tab | `<!-- new tab -->` | Generative | Tablet: a pause to think, then a blank tab; the next web page is typed into it. |
| Back | `<!-- back -->` | Generative | Tablet: back to the page before, scrolled where it was left. An unread page is glanced down first. Follow it with a mark, not text. |
| Redirect | `<!-- redirect -->` | Generative | Tablet: put it before a url - the tap (or typed address) that reaches that page is sent through a chain of redirects the reader never asked for, the address bar jumping through them on its own. Bare: six hops made up from the page's own site, a scam's funnel. Or name them, comma-separated. |
| Notification | `<!-- notify: Sender \| Subject \| A line of the message -->` | Generative | Tablet: a notification banner drops from the top of the screen a moment after the reading reaches this point - mid-paragraph or on a line of its own - holds a few seconds and slides away: an email arriving. Sender | subject | preview. Not read aloud; the voice does not wait for it. |
| Landscape | `<!-- landscape -->` | Generative | Tablet: turn to landscape. The camera turns; the tablet stays where it lies. |
| Portrait | `<!-- portrait -->` | Generative | Tablet: turn back to portrait. |
| Skip | `<!-- skip -->` | Generative | Tablet: shown, not read. Mid-paragraph, the rest of it from the end of that sentence; on its own line, the whole paragraph below. |
| Placeholder stories | `<!-- filler: 3 -->` | Generative | Tablet: this many placeholder stories - squiggles where writing would be - on the page here. |

## The deck

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| The deck | `## Cards` | Table | Opens the show's own deck: every list item under this heading, down to the next heading of its level, is a card, and each episode's cards are a seeded shuffle of them. A brief with no such section leaves each episode's cards to the producer. |
| A suit | `### Major Arcana` | Table | Inside the deck: names the group the cards listed under it belong to - a suit, an arcana, a team. |
| A card | `- The Tower: sudden upheaval, a structure that was never sound` | Table | Inside the deck: one card - its name, then what it means after a colon. A numeral may lead it (XVI. The Tower). A writer is handed a card's meaning only once that card is drawn. |

## Letter

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thought | `*She is always fine.*` | Generative | Letter: a paragraph in italics, whole, is a thought - said, and never written: the writer stops and thinks it, the pen lifted. |
| Strike | `<!-- strike -->` | Generative | Letter: the writer stops to decide, then the pen crosses out the paragraph it last wrote, every line of it. The pause is about 3 seconds; strike: 5 makes it 5. |
| Struck words | `<!-- struck: morning -->` | Generative | Letter: inside a written line, these words are written and said first - then the writer stops to decide, crosses out just these words, and writes the words after the mark beside them. |
| Ink | `<!-- color: red -->` | Generative | Letter: the pen's ink from here on - red, blue, green, purple, brown, black, a hex color, or default for the desk's own. Each ink is a pen of its own lying by the pad; the writer puts one down and picks up the other, and inside a written line goes on beside where it stopped. |
| Written, not said | `<!-- unspoken: Dear Ink, -->` | Generative | Letter: the pen writes this and the voice does not say it - it waits while it is written. On a line of its own, a line; inside a written line, words in it (a correction beside struck words). |
| Timed sketch | `<!-- sketch (10s): a tree of small dots -->` | Generative | Letter: a sketch drawn in at most this many seconds, the pen paced to take that long - without a time a big one is dashed off in about 5. One with less ink is drawn at the hand's own pace. |
| Point | `<!-- point: sketch, the dot -->` | Generative | Letter: inside what is said, at the next word the pen points at the last sketch - or at the part of it so described - until the sentence ends. point: camera lifts the pen to whoever is watching. |
| Tap | `<!-- tap -->` | Generative | Letter: the pen is turned over and its top tapped on the pad - tap: desk, on the desk beside it - while the writer thinks. The voice waits a moment; the taps run on under the next words. |
| Picture ends | `<!-- /image -->` | Generative | Letter: ends the passage a picture is shown over - from its image mark to here the picture fills the screen, slowly moving, while the voice reads on and the pen writes on unseen; then the desk comes back. An image mark straight after it, or before it, dissolves into its own picture instead, the page never seen between. |
| Hold still | `<!-- still -->` | Generative | Letter: from here to the next written line the camera holds dead still on the last sketch, and the pen is taken off the page - for something the viewer does on the screen. |
| New page | `<!-- new page -->` | Generative | Letter: the next writing starts a page of its own (a page also turns by itself once it is full). |

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Note to self | `<!-- a note to yourself -->` | Generative, Synthesis, Table | Any other HTML comment is an authoring note: never spoken, never printed. **In a Table brief:** Any other HTML comment is a note to yourself: taken out of the brief before any agent is handed it. |
